# M3.9 -- prove a bot can kill something AND LOOT ITS CORPSE.
#
# COPY of m39_hunt_armed.txt (do not edit that file) with a looting attempt
# appended after the kill. Everything through "say the fight is over" is
# unchanged from m39_hunt_armed.txt; see that file's comments for why an
# armed fresh fighter, why real wilderness and not a farm, and why the wolf
# body ids below are read from the CHARDEF headers rather than generic UO
# documentation.
#
# RUN AS AN ARMED FIGHTER SESSION (53+ / RevolutionFighter03+).
#
# ============================================================================
# A CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS DRAFT OF THIS FILE, FOUND BY READING THE
# SERVER, NOT JUST THE CLIENT
#
# The previous draft (and the milestone brief itself) assumed a wolf corpse
# simply "holds" its RESOURCES=1 i_ribs_raw,6 i_hide the moment it dies. That
# is wrong, and a live run (loot7, 2026-08-27 22:50:18) caught it in the act:
# `open @corpse` right after the kill answered
#     [0x3C] container contents: 0 item(s)
# on a corpse that had just been created by a fame-granting kill seconds
# earlier. That is not a bug in the client or a wrong-corpse mixup -- it is
# Source-X's own carving rule, read from the server source itself:
#
#   CChar::MakeCorpse (server/Source-X/src/game/items/CItemCorpse.cpp:168)
#   only calls DropAll(pCorpse) -- it moves whatever the CREATURE was
#   physically carrying into the corpse. RESOURCES is never touched here.
#
#   RESOURCES only materializes via CChar::Use_CarveCorpse
#   (server/Source-X/src/game/chars/CCharUse.cpp:49), which is reached by
#   double-clicking a bladed weapon/tool (armed the "use item -> target"
#   cursor) and then targeting the corpse:
#   CClient::OnTarg_Use_Item's big switch on the USED item's type
#   (server/Source-X/src/game/clients/CClientTarg.cpp:1691) has
#     case IT_WEAPON_MACE_SHARP: case IT_WEAPON_FENCE:
#     case IT_WEAPON_AXE: case IT_WEAPON_SWORD:   // ~line 1885
#   falling through (when the target isn't a char) to
#     switch (m_pChar->CanTouchStatic(&pt, id, pItemTarg)) { case IT_CORPSE:
#         m_pChar->Use_CarveCorpse(pCorpse, pItemUse); }   // ~line 1957
#   which walks CCharBase::m_BaseResources (i.e. the CHARDEF's RESOURCES=
#   line) and calls pCorpse->ContentAdd(pPart) for each part -- ONLY THEN do
#   the meat and hide actually exist as items inside the corpse container.
#
# i_katana (ITEMDEF 013fe, items/weapons/i_weapons.scp:966) is
# TYPE=t_weapon_sword, which is exactly IT_WEAPON_SWORD -- the same weapon
# this fighter is already carrying to fight with is also the tool that
# carves the kill. No new equipment, no new mechanic outside what a real
# player does: a sword doubles as a knife for this purpose on Source-X.
#
# So this scenario now does what m39_hunt_armed.txt's draft sibling did not:
# it OPENS the corpse once to show it is empty on arrival (a real, provable
# fact about this shard, not an oversight), CARVES it with the same blade
# that made the kill (`use @blade` / `wait_target` / `target @corpse`,
# structurally identical to m37_slice_b_minoc.txt's `use @hammer` /
# `wait_target` / `target @ingots` forging step -- both are
# "use-an-equipped-tool-then-target-something" through the same client
# ActionUseObject -> wait_target -> ActionTargetObject path), then re-opens
# it to prove RESOURCES now exist as real, serialised items.
#
# THE GAP THAT STILL STANDS AFTER THIS FIX
#
# Carving solves "does the loot exist" but not "can THIS scenario file get it
# into the bot's pack". That second problem is real and is exactly what the
# previous draft found, unchanged by the carving discovery above -- read
# src/bot/Scenario.cpp's `remember` handling (the pack_graphic /
# carried_graphic / world_graphic / mobile_* branches, Scenario.cpp:1055-
# 1130) and Client::FindItem's SearchZone enum (Client.h:1154) end to end:
#
#   kZoneBackpack -- ALWAYS PlayerEquipSerialAt(kLayerBackpack), i.e. the
#                    bot's OWN worn backpack. Never an arbitrary container.
#   kZoneEquip    -- the bot's own worn gear.
#   kZoneWorld    -- top-level dynamic items_ (things lying directly on the
#                    ground), which is how `world_graphic` finds the corpse
#                    ITSELF -- but a corpse's CONTENTS (raw meat, hide, once
#                    carved) live in a second map keyed by container serial
#                    (containerItems_[corpse_serial], populated by the 0x3C
#                    handler, Client.cpp:1398-1435) that nothing in the
#                    scenario Op set can search.
#
# `pack_graphic`/`carried_graphic` are hard-wired to the PLAYER's own
# backpack serial specifically (Client::FindBackpackItemByGraphic,
# Client::FindItemByGraphic both call PlayerEquipSerialAt(kLayerBackpack)
# directly, confirmed at Client.cpp:2577-2585 and the equivalent
# FindItemByGraphic) -- there is no "pack_graphic, but for THIS container"
# variant, and Scenario::Resolve()'s token grammar (Scenario.cpp:147-195:
# @name, self, backpack, bank, vendor*, vendor_sell_graphic:<hex>,
# vendor_graphic:<hex>, a bare hex/decimal literal) has nothing that reads
# containerItems_ for a bound-but-not-the-backpack serial either. A corpse's
# item serials are assigned by the server at carve time, so they cannot be
# hardcoded as a literal the way a vendor's stock can be named by graphic.
#
# THIS IS DOUBLY BLOCKED, WORSE THAN THE PREVIOUS DRAFT REALISED. The
# capability to do this DOES exist in this codebase --
# Client::SendTakeToBackpack(serial, qty) (Client.h:684, "lift item from ANY
# open container -> backpack") and the containerItems_ map itself -- but
# BOTH are declared in the PRIVATE section of class Client (past the
# `private:` at Client.h:568; the only access is `friend struct
# js::ClientBindings`, Client.h:571, which is how the JS scripting layer's
# Player.take(serial, qty) / Player.containerItems(serial)
# (src/js/ClientBindings.cpp:524-556) reaches them). Scenario (bot::Scenario)
# is not that friend. So even the smallest possible fix -- a new `remember
# container_graphic <bind> <graphic-list>` op living entirely inside
# Scenario.cpp, reading only Client's already-public surface -- CANNOT be
# written today: there is no public Client method that exposes an arbitrary
# container's contents, and adding one means touching Client.h, which this
# milestone's brief says is locked ("I am editing src/Client.h ... RIGHT
# NOW. Do not touch those."). And the JS scripting path that already has the
# capability is never wired to a launch route: local/dev/run_m25.ps1 only
# ever passes `--scenario X.txt`.
#
# So this file proves everything that CAN be proven with the existing Op set
# -- kill, corpse, empty-on-arrival, carve, corpse now non-empty with the
# right graphics inside it -- and stops, deliberately, at the one line that
# would require editing a file this task was told not to touch.
# ============================================================================

wait_world
sleep 2500

# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. resurrect if dead
# CORRECTION: the brief describes m39_hunt_armed.txt as "resurrects at a
# healer if needed", but that file (read in full before writing this copy)
# has no such step -- it assumes a living character. Fighter03 was in fact
# dead on disk when this file was first run (loot8, 2026-08-27 23:17: login
# arrived as body 0x0192 with "Your ghostly hand passes through the
# object.", i.e. still a ghost from an earlier fight this same session), so
# this scenario cannot skip the step the way its namesake does.
#
# The established idiom for this, used identically in m39_hunt.txt and
# m39_pvm_recover.txt: walk to a wandering healer and acknowledge the 0x2C
# ghost menu. Replying to 0x2C does not resurrect by itself
# (src/network/receive.cpp:616-639) -- a healer NPC raises a ghost it
# notices on its own (CChar::NPC_LookAtCharHealer,
# server/Source-X/src/game/chars/CCharNPCAct.cpp:895-937). If the character
# is already alive these three steps are harmless: `resurrect` returns
# invalid_state and `wait_alive` passes immediately (documented in
# m39_hunt.txt's own header).
travel_service healer
wait_travel
sleep 4000
resurrect
wait_action
sleep 2000
wait_alive
say alive and ready to hunt

ensure_peace
gait run

request_skills
sleep 1500
skill_report

remember pack backpack
open @pack
wait_action
sleep 1500

# ------------------------------------------------------------- 1. arm ourself
remember blade pack_graphic 0x13FE,0x13FF
require blade
equip @blade 1
wait_action
sleep 2000
say armed

# --------------------------------------------------- 2. out to REAL wilderness
use_moongates on
travel_point 1265 1612
wait_travel
expect_travel ok
sleep 2000

say hunting wolves

# --------------------------------------------------------------- 3. find prey
# 0x0019 grey wolf  0x00E1 timber wolf  0x0017 dire wolf  0x0025 white wolf
# 0x003F cougar     0x00D6 panther -- read off the CHARDEF headers, see
# m39_hunt_armed.txt for the full history of why.
#
# CHASE-AS-YOU-GO, unlike m39_hunt_armed.txt's own sweep. loot9
# (2026-08-27 23:30) proved live why this matters even though the base file
# gets away with a single remember at the end of the sweep: a Cougar
# (0x0000B474, body 0x003F -- a valid prey id) was sighted at (1229,1655)
# and again at (1210,1680), but the ONE `remember prey` this file used to
# run only after the LAST waypoint (1185,1698, which is farm/NPC territory --
# "Ledah", "Tano, the rancher", "Cat", "Rat") saw nothing eligible nearby and
# bound 0x00000000, discarding an animal that had been in view twice. So:
# after every scan, try to bind prey and immediately try goto_mobile toward
# it. goto_mobile on an unbound (0x00000000) serial is a documented no-op
# (Client::ActionGotoMobile logs "not in the mobile cache" and returns false
# without starting an action), so this costs nothing on legs where nothing
# is sighted, and on the leg where something IS sighted it turns the bot
# toward it instead of continuing away.
scan_mobiles
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1265 1612
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1272 1607
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1229 1655
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1210 1680
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
goto 1185 1698
wait_goto
scan_mobiles
sleep 800
remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
goto_mobile @prey
wait_action

# The sweep is done. If something was ever sighted, the chases above have
# been closing on it the whole time; give it a few more scan/chase cycles to
# close the last distance and settle in the mobile cache before the hard
# `require`.
loop 4
  scan_mobiles
  sleep 1200
  remember prey mobile_body 0x0019,0x00E1,0x0017,0x0025,0x003F,0x00D6
  goto_mobile @prey
  wait_action
endloop

require prey

goto_mobile @prey
wait_action
sleep 1500

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ 4. kill it
mark_hp

war on
sleep 800
attack @prey
wait_action

loop 20
  goto_mobile @prey
  wait_action
  sleep 2500
endloop

scan_mobiles
sleep 2500

war off
sleep 1200
say the fight is over

# --------------------------------------------------------- 5. find the corpse
# i_corpse is ITEMDEF 02006 (runtime/scripts/items/i_char_icons.scp:20-27),
# and every corpse in the shard is created from this ONE item, so 0x2006 is
# not a guess and not per-creature the way the wolf body ids above are.
#
# No travel step here on purpose: the attack loop above re-issued
# goto_mobile every 2.5s to stay in melee range for the whole fight, so the
# corpse should spawn within container-open range of wherever the bot is
# standing when the loop ends. goto takes a literal x/y and travel_entity
# resolves only MOBILE serials via Client::MobilePosition
# (ClientTravel.cpp:254-265) -- a corpse is a world item, not in
# mobileCache_, so neither could get us there if this open failed on range.
open @pack
wait_action
sleep 1000

remember corpse world_graphic 0x2006
require corpse

open @corpse
wait_action
sleep 2000
say corpse found, checking it before carving

# -------------------------------------------- 6. PROVE it is empty on arrival
# This is the finding the previous draft of this file missed: nothing has
# touched RESOURCES yet, so the corpse should currently be reported as
# holding 0 (or, at most, whatever loose junk the wolf happened to be
# "wearing", which for a wild animal is nothing) items. The evidence is the
# unconditional log line from Client::OnContainerContents:
#     [0x3C] container contents: N item(s)
# Read N here in the log; it is expected to be 0.

# ------------------------------------------------- 7. CARVE IT WITH THE BLADE
# The katana that made the kill (TYPE=t_weapon_sword, ITEMDEF 013fe) is also
# a valid carving tool on Source-X: CClientTarg.cpp's OnTarg_Use_Item routes
# IT_WEAPON_SWORD (falling through when the target is not a char) into
# CanTouchStatic's IT_CORPSE case, which calls Use_CarveCorpse(pCorpse,
# pItemUse) -- pItemUse being whatever was double-clicked, here the blade.
# This is structurally the same "use an equipped tool, then target
# something" sequence m37_slice_b_minoc.txt already proved with the smith's
# hammer (`use @hammer` / `wait_target` / `target @ingots`), just aimed at a
# corpse instead of a pile of ingots.
use @blade
wait_target
target @corpse
sleep 3000
say carved

# ------------------------------------------ 8. RE-OPEN AND PROVE IT IS FULL
# Use_CarveCorpse walks the wolf's own CHARDEF RESOURCES=1 i_ribs_raw,6
# i_hide (npcs/c_monster_classic.scp:1215) and ContentAdd()s each part
# straight into the corpse container. Re-opening (the same pattern
# m37_slice_b_minoc.txt uses after mining/smelting to force a fresh 0x3C
# dump rather than trust a stale one) should now show a non-zero count, and
# graphically the new items should be 0x09F1 (i_ribs_raw,
# items/i_profession_cook_barkeep_baker.scp:990) and 0x1078/0x1079
# (i_hide/its pile DUPELIST, items/i_profession_tailor_tanner.scp:348).
open @corpse
wait_action
sleep 2000

say corpse carved, meat and hide should now be inside it -- reachable by no scenario op

# --------------------------------------------------- 9. THE STEP THAT STILL DOES NOT EXIST
#
# The brief's own instruction: prove the transfer with mark_item before and
# expect_item_gain after, the way m37_slice_b_minoc.txt does for smelted
# ingots. That pattern needs a `move <item-in-corpse> <amount> @pack` line,
# and <item-in-corpse> needs a `remember` mode that searches
# containerItems_[@corpse] by graphic (0x09F1 ribs, 0x1078/0x1079 hide) the
# same way `pack_graphic` searches containerItems_[player's own backpack].
# That remember mode does not exist, and per the header above, it cannot be
# added without touching Client.h (to expose containerItems_ or
# SendTakeToBackpack beyond the js::ClientBindings friend), which this
# milestone explicitly forbids editing right now. Writing
#     remember loot pack_graphic 0x09F1,0x1078,0x1079
# here would not be that mode; pack_graphic ignores @corpse entirely and
# would search the PLAYER'S OWN backpack, silently binding whatever ribs/
# hide the bot happens to already be carrying (nothing, for this fighter) --
# exactly the kind of invented, misleading workaround the brief said not to
# build. So this scenario stops here, deliberately, with the fight, the
# empty corpse, the carve, and the now-full corpse all proven, and only the
# final pack-transfer left undone because the file it needs touched is
# locked for this task.

request_skills
sleep 1500
skill_report
sleep 1500
logout
